facts.value: An ancient report says Ptolemy imprisoned the Alexandrian scholar Aristophanes of Byzantium on suspicion of leaving for Pergamon.
facts.quote: is said to have imprisoned Aristophanes of Byzantium
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://penelope.uchicago.edu/encyclopaedia_romana/greece/paganism/pergamumlibrary.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'is said to have imprisoned Aristophanes of Byzantium'

facts.value: Crates of Mallus, a scholar from Pergamon, fell into a Roman sewer opening around 169 BC while on an embassy. He broke his leg.
facts.quote: as an envoy to the Senate in about 169 BC, he fell into a sewer opening and broke his leg
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://penelope.uchicago.edu/encyclopaedia_romana/greece/paganism/pergamumlibrary.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'he fell into a sewer opening and broke his leg'

facts.value: Strabo writes that the heirs of Neleus, who held the books of Aristotle and Theophrastus, hid them in a trench to keep them from the Attalid book-hunters. Moisture and moths damaged them.
facts.quote: in a kind of trench. But much later, when the books had been damaged by moisture and moths
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Strabo/13A3*.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'in a kind of trench. But much later, when the books had been damaged by moisture and moths'

facts.value: Pliny reports a story that Ptolemy banned papyrus exports and that parchment (charta pergamena) was invented at Pergamon as a substitute. The same page notes Herodotus says animal skins were used for writing long before.
facts.quote: parchment ( charta pergamena ) was said to have been invented in Pergamon as a substitute
facts.check: curl -sL -A 'Mozilla/5.0' 'https://penelope.uchicago.edu/encyclopaedia_romana/greece/paganism/pergamumlibrary.html' | perl -0pe 's/<[^>]*>/ /g;s/\s+/ /g' | rg -o -m1 -F 'parchment ( charta pergamena ) was said to have been invented in Pergamon as a substitute'

facts.value: The rooms on the Athena terrace long taken for the royal library may not have been one. Later scholars have suggested a reception hall, a store for offerings or a display room.
facts.quote: It therefore is not certain that the rooms originally thought to have been the location of the Pergamon Library actually served that purpose
